body_markdown:
An Indian business collecting global payments has to decide who will be the seller on each transaction. A Merchant of Record (MoR) is the legal seller for the transactions it covers, taking on agreed payment and tax responsibilities under its contract. An international payment gateway enables collection while your business remains the seller.


Choose Razorpay International’s payment-acceptance products when you want to collect from overseas customers, retain control of the sale, and manage the obligations that remain yours. Consider a contracted third-party MoR when eligible global sales need covered indirect-tax and seller services handled by someone else. Neither choice is automatically better for every Indian business.


This guide compares the two on seller identity, tax ownership, payment methods, recurring billing, export documentation and full operating cost. The right answer changes depending on whether you run self-serve SaaS, issue B2B invoices, or sell to both domestic and international buyers.


## Key Takeaways


- **For global SaaS with recurring billing and compliance handled:** Choose Razorpay International with Razorpay Subscriptions when your eligible account supports the required international card flow and your business will remain the seller, managing applicable taxes and export records. Choose a contracted MoR when your priority is outsourcing covered seller and destination-market tax responsibilities. Confirm recurring-billing features and contractual coverage separately.
- **For export-led SaaS and service businesses:** Evaluate Razorpay international cards for online checkout and International Bank Transfer for overseas B2B invoice receipts. Match the buyer’s payment rail, currency and invoice workflow to the product. Confirm activation, purpose codes, buyer details, settlement conditions and the receipt document available for that method. An invoice bank transfer is not an automatic recurring debit.
- **For a SaaS CTO seeking global recurring payments with built-in dunning:** Razorpay Subscriptions documents international-currency card subscriptions, scheduled retries on T+1, T+2 and T+3, webhooks and customer recovery notifications. UPI and Emandate subscriptions are INR-only. Test failed renewals, pending and halted events, card updates and your access rules before rollout; payment recovery does not transfer global tax responsibility.
- **For export documentation and compliance:** FIRS records and method-specific export documents support reconciliation and the receipt trail. They do not alone establish export tax treatment. An MoR contract also leaves your Indian business with accounting and records for its own supply and receipts. Confirm the current reporting and realisation requirements with your Authorised Dealer bank and advisers.
- **For the true cost of collecting global payments:** Compare processing, MoR services, billing and tax tools, FX, refunds, disputes and retained operational work together. Check what each quote already includes so you do not count processing twice. Use the approved account settlement schedule and the actual event that starts the clock; headline fees or payout numbers are incomplete.
- **For the final gateway-versus-MoR decision:** Select by product, buyer type, payment method and responsibility ownership. Razorpay’s standard international gateway arrangement keeps your business as seller; a separate MoR arrangement depends on its product, contracting entity, availability and eligible sales. A mixed setup can serve distinct sales flows when the additional contracts and reconciliation work are justified.


## What Is the Difference Between Razorpay International and a Merchant of Record?


With Razorpay’s international payment-acceptance arrangement, your business remains the seller and uses payment infrastructure to collect overseas revenue. A contracted third-party Merchant of Record becomes the seller for covered transactions and assumes specified transaction responsibilities. The choice depends on which obligations you want to retain and which you want to outsource.


### Payment Acceptance and Seller Responsibility


Two flows make the distinction concrete.


Under direct collection, your customer in Berlin buys from your Indian company. Your invoice, your refund policy and your tax position apply. Razorpay’s[international payment acceptance](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) moves the money and settles it to your account.


Under a contracted MoR arrangement, the designated MoR entity becomes the seller for covered transactions. Razorpay’s published[Terms of Use for International Orders](https://razorpay.com/mor_terms/) illustrate a resale model involving Razorpay Inc. and shipped items sold to buyers outside India. Those terms should not be treated as the contract for standard Razorpay gateway collections or proof of general SaaS MoR availability. Confirm the exact product, contracting entity and eligible sales.


Avoid two oversimplifications. A payment aggregator is not merely a data pipe that cannot support settlement or export records. And a payment-provider authorisation, such as Razorpay’s RBI PA-CB listing, does not by itself transfer your seller obligations. Payment authorisation, seller identity and tax responsibility are three separate questions.


### Compare Responsibilities Before Features


Decision area Razorpay International payment acceptance Contracted third-party MoR


Seller to the end buyer Your business remains the seller. The MoR is the seller for covered transactions.


Payment collection Enabled international cards, local methods or bank-transfer collection, depending on product. Methods and markets supported by that MoR.


Destination-market transaction taxes Your business assesses and manages applicable obligations, with advisers or tooling where needed. Covered obligations handled by the MoR under its agreement.


Recurring billing Native subscription capability or an additional billing layer, based on verified requirements. Subscription features depend on the MoR; seller status alone does not establish feature depth.


Indian business records Your business reconciles invoices, receipts, fees and relevant export documents. Your business reconciles the MoR contract, its supply to the MoR, deductions and payouts.


Refunds and disputes Your business retains seller obligations and uses available provider workflows. Managed within the MoR arrangement; confirm deductions, evidence duties and exclusions.


Checkout and customer operations Your business controls its chosen implementation within product rules. Check checkout options, buyer documents, support ownership and data portability.


Cost comparison Include collection, billing or tax services and retained operating work. Check which services are bundled, plus any extras, FX and payout conditions.


## Which Model Fits Your Indian Business?


Direct international collection can suit an Indian business that wants to remain the seller and can manage the associated tax and operational work. A third-party MoR can suit eligible products where outsourcing covered seller responsibilities is genuinely valuable. Invoice-led exports need a separate assessment of bank transfers, documentation and reconciliation.


### Global SaaS and Digital Products


Direct collection fits when you have confirmed international subscription support on your account, you want control over checkout and customer data, and you have a workable plan for applicable destination taxes, refunds and customer records.


An MoR fits when your product is eligible under the contract, you sell to many self-serve buyers across jurisdictions, and outsourcing covered indirect-tax obligations removes real work. Confirm product category, country coverage, billing features and contract scope first. Do not pick a model purely because the company is early stage, and do not treat any revenue number as a universal switching threshold.


### Agencies, Consultants and B2B Invoices


For invoice-led exporters, the buyer’s preferred local bank rail and the invoice reference on the remittance usually matter more than subscription checkout. A finance team in London paying against a purchase order wants a local transfer instruction, not a card page.


International bank transfers are a direct-collection option with their own activation, purpose-code and documentation conditions. A bank transfer is not an automatic recurring debit mandate, so do not plan renewals around it.


### Mixed Domestic and International Sales


A mixed model can separate domestic INR collection, global self-serve sales and enterprise invoices when those three flows genuinely differ in buyer behaviour and contract structure.


It also adds work: separate seller contracts, different invoice formats, split refund paths, subscription records in more than one system, and reconciliation across multiple settlement streams. Hybrid architecture is neither always necessary nor rarely useful. Scope it deliberately.


## How Razorpay Supports International Collections


Razorpay documents international cards, local payment methods and international bank transfers for Indian businesses, subject to the applicable product and account activation. Choose the method around how your customer prefers to pay, the supported currency and your business category. These capabilities enable collection. They do not, by themselves, make Razorpay the seller of your product.


### International Cards and Local Payment Methods


Card acceptance requires an active KYC-verified account, and the international feature is enabled only after banking-partner approval, with policy pages published on your site and some business categories excluded. Razorpay’s own[onboarding requirements guide](https://razorpay.com/learn/breaking-down-the-requirements-for-accepting-international-payments-through-razorpay/) adds that full domestic activation comes first, and that invoices, bank statements, prior settlement reports and category certificates such as FSSAI, IATA or RERA may be requested as supporting evidence.


Check the supported currency and method list for your account rather than relying on a marketing currency count. A headline number for card acceptance is not proof that every method or subscription configuration supports the same list. Local payment methods carry their own country and enablement checks. Start with[international card payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/international-card-payments/) to confirm what applies to you.


### International Bank Transfers for Export Receipts


Razorpay’s[International Bank Transfer](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/bank-transfers/) product provides local-currency virtual accounts so overseas buyers can pay through rails such as ACH, FPS, SEPA, NPP and EFT, with SWIFT where supported, settling to your Indian account. The[documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-bank-transfer) lists prerequisites including a KYC-verified account, business PAN, and an eligible export purpose code such as P0802 for software consultancy or P1006 for management consultancy.


Invoice and buyer details are prerequisites for settlement in the documented flows. Physical-goods exports may need additional shipment evidence.


> **DID YOU KNOW:** A local foreign-currency collection account and an EEFC account are different arrangements. The bank-transfer documentation says funds cannot simply be held in the local collection account, while describing a separate EEFC settlement option.[EEFC retention](https://razorpay.com/blog/what-is-an-eefc-account/) is also conditional and time-bound under RBI rules. Confirm which account you are actually using.


## Can You Collect Global SaaS Subscriptions with Razorpay?


Razorpay Subscriptions documents plan-based recurring billing, automated invoices, retries and webhooks. Its FAQ allows card subscriptions in supported international currencies, while UPI and eMandate subscriptions are INR-only. Confirm international activation, supported cards and the actual billing model before building. Recurring collection and global tax responsibility remain separate decisions.


### Match the Currency to the Recurring Method


Razorpay’s[Subscriptions FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs?preferred-country=IN) documents card payments in supported international currencies, with settlement in INR under that flow. UPI and Emandate subscriptions support INR. UPI AutoPay should not be used to debit a USD or EUR subscription.


Before rollout, confirm the supported card networks, currency, merchant category and international activation for your account. Check these against the recurring flow you intend to use. Razorpay’s guide to[international subscription payments](https://razorpay.com/blog/international-subscriptions-india/) explains the recurring-card collection model for eligible accounts.


Keep three things distinct: one-time international checkout, plan-based[Razorpay Subscriptions](https://razorpay.com/subscriptions/) , and merchant-triggered recurring payments. A country or currency count for one does not prove support for the others.


### What Native Retries Actually Do


Razorpay documents[scheduled card-payment reattempts](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/payment-retries) on T+1, T+2 and T+3 after a failed charge, with the subscription moving to pending and then to halted if retries fail. Webhooks notify your application about pending and halted subscriptions, and failure emails link to payment-method recovery. Plan around this documented recovery flow and do not assume that every failed renewal will be recovered.


Dunning is the wider process of recovering overdue recurring payments. Retries are one component of it.


Use the webhook events to make your own access and grace-period decisions. The documentation is explicit that invoices for halted subscriptions still get created but are not charged automatically, so someone has to own that follow-up. Customer notifications can also occur during failure recovery, not only after halting, and a hosted recovery page is not the same thing as a newly created payment link.


### When an Additional Billing or Tax Layer Helps


Evaluate requirements one at a time: billing schedules, international-currency cards, mid-cycle plan changes, invoice generation, retry behaviour and application entitlements. A specialist billing or tax layer may help when verified requirements exceed the native flow. Do not assume the integration already exists, and do not assume every business needs one.


If your billing model needs add-ons, usage metering or proration, confirm the current capability for your configuration before relying on it. A billing or tax tool does not automatically become the legal seller; that remains a contractual question.


> **PRO TIP:** Test the full renewal path before rollout: initial authorisation, a successful renewal, a failed charge, each documented retry, payment-method recovery and your application’s response to pending or halted states. A successful first payment does not establish the renewal flow.


## What Indian Export and Tax Responsibilities Remain?


Under a gateway arrangement, your business remains responsible for assessing and managing applicable transaction taxes. A contracted MoR can handle the transaction-tax duties it covers. Either way, the Indian entity needs appropriate accounting and export records for its own supply and receipts.


### Separate Foreign Transaction Taxes from Indian Export Records


Foreign VAT, GST and sales-tax obligations depend on where your customer is located, what you sell and whether the sale is to a business or consumer. Map the applicable obligations for your actual markets and transactions. For EU sales, consult the[European Commission’s VAT One Stop Shop guidance](https://vat-one-stop-shop.ec.europa.eu/index_en) for the relevant scheme. Do not assume that one revenue threshold or a tax tool covers every jurisdiction.


A tax-calculation tool and a legal reseller arrangement are different services. Establish which party calculates, collects, files and remits for each sale. Under an MoR arrangement, confirm who your Indian entity supplies, what it invoices, and what documentation accompanies the payout.


### What Export-of-Services Conditions Mean


Section 2(6) of the IGST Act sets several conditions that must be met together: supplier in India, recipient outside India, place of supply outside India, payment received in convertible foreign exchange or in rupees where RBI permits, and the two parties not being mere establishments of the same person. CBIC has issued a circular clarifying the payment condition specifically.


Do not treat a FIRC alone as the legal test for zero rating or an MoR contract as automatic GST or FEMA compliance. Confirm your export declaration, receipt records and applicable realisation period with your Authorised Dealer bank. The RBI rules in force from 1 October 2026, as subsequently amended, include different conditions and deemed-submission arrangements for specified service-export receipts. Apply the current requirements to your own flow.


> **DID YOU KNOW:** Export-of-services status involves several statutory conditions. Receiving an export-related statement helps document a receipt, but it does not independently establish that every tax condition has been met.


## How Do You Receive Funds and Export Documents?


Reconcile the customer invoice, buyer details, purpose code, gross receipt, fees, conversion and bank settlement. Razorpay documents: downloadable bank FIRS certificates and Razorpay-generated statements. Confirm which record your bank or accountant requires. Settlement timing and document type vary by product and flow.


### Build a Traceable Receipt-to-Invoice Record


Build one row per receipt covering invoice number, buyer legal name and country, service description, purpose code, payment reference, gross amount and currency, provider fees and tax on fees, FX details, net INR settlement reference, and the document type available.


Razorpay’s[FIRS documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/firs) describes two sections in the Dashboard: certificates provided by the bank, and Razorpay-generated statements that act as an alternative, along with a purpose-code update process. That does not justify promising a bank eFIRC for every card transaction. Bank-transfer materials use FIRC and FIRS terminology in different places, so confirm the required document and its availability for your selected rail.


### Confirm the Settlement Clock


For international card collections, check the settlement schedule approved for your account in the Razorpay Dashboard, as directed by the[International Payments FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/faqs?preferred-country=IN) , and your[applicable agreement](https://razorpay.com/terms/) . For the documented[bank-transfer flow](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-bank-transfer) , confirm the T+1 starting event against invoice capture or invoice-details submission and complete the required checks. MoR payouts have their own schedules, reserves and conditions. Compare the product, starting event, working-day calendar and any holds together.


> **PRO TIP:** Ask for a worked settlement statement for your intended flow. Match the gross sale, any taxes collected, fees, FX, refunds and the net bank receipt. Confirm the document type and the event that starts the settlement clock.


## What Does Each Global Payment Model Cost?


Compare payment processing, any MoR service fee, billing and tax tools, FX, refunds, dispute charges and retained operational work. An MoR quote may already include processing, so do not add it twice. Confirm your applicable commercial quote before calculating any saving.


### Compare Equivalent Services


Current[International Payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) marketing advertises 1% for bank transfers and up to 3% for cards, with asterisked conditions. Treat those as dated headline claims and confirm the terms and your applicable rate. Do not call 3% a universal all-in rate, do not present bank-transfer pricing as card pricing, and do not apply a domestic promotional offer to international payments.


Check GST on provider fees, FX terms, subscription charges, refund treatment and dispute charges separately. Do not compare a bare gateway fee with a bundled MoR quote and call the gap pure savings. The direct seller still pays for the work the bundle would have covered.


### A Worked Cost Comparison


Illustration only: assumed rates on Rs 10,00,000 monthly sales, before taxes on fees, FX, refunds, disputes, reserves and other unlisted costs. This is arithmetic for decision-making, not Razorpay pricing, a commercial quote or an industry benchmark. No named provider is represented by either assumed rate. Let R be the direct seller’s monthly cost of the services and operating work needed to make the comparison equivalent.


Cost line Assumed direct-collection quote Assumed MoR bundle quote


Monthly sales base Rs 10,00,000 Rs 10,00,000


Assumed percentage charge 3% 5%, assumed to include processing


Percentage charge in rupees Rs 30,000 Rs 50,000


Equivalent additional seller services and work R Confirm what the bundle includes and excludes


Comparison before remaining adjustments Rs 30,000 + R Rs 50,000 plus any exclusions


The percentage-charge gap is Rs 20,000. If R were Rs 10,000 and all other relevant costs were equal, the illustrative direct total would be Rs 40,000. If R were Rs 25,000, it would be Rs 55,000. The result changes with actual scope, quotes and costs. This example establishes no real-world saving and no break-even volume.


## Which Global Payment Model Should You Choose?


There is no universal winner. Match the requirement to the model, then verify before committing.


If your main requirement is… Evaluate first Confirm before deciding


Direct international checkout while remaining the seller Razorpay international card acceptance Merchant eligibility, methods, currencies, fees and retained tax duties.


Overseas B2B invoice collection Razorpay International Bank Transfer Buyer payment rail, invoice requirements, account eligibility, settlement event and export document.


Global subscriptions with your own seller and tax operations Razorpay Subscriptions with the intended international configuration Cards and currency, activation, renewal recovery and any additional billing requirements.


Covered foreign transaction-tax and seller services outsourced Contracted third-party MoR Eligible product, legal seller, markets, tax coverage, payouts, documents and exclusions.


Different needs across domestic, global self-serve and enterprise sales A deliberately scoped mixed model Separate contracts, invoice identity, refunds, reconciliation and subscription ownership.


**Practical decision sequence:**


1. Identify what you sell and whether customers are businesses or consumers.
2. List customer countries, payment preferences and one-time versus recurring charges.
3. Choose who should be the seller for each sale and document the responsibilities retained.
4. Verify product eligibility, currencies, recurring methods and the actual funds flow.
5. Confirm taxes, invoices, export records, refunds, disputes and payout conditions with the responsible owners.
6. Compare equivalent commercial quotes, services and operating work.
7. Test collection, renewal failure and recovery, and reconciliation before rollout.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Razorpay International a Merchant of Record?


Razorpay’s international gateway arrangement enables payment acceptance while your business remains the seller. This article compares that arrangement with a contracted third-party MoR. Razorpay also markets a separate[Merchant of Record offering](https://razorpay.com/merchant-of-record/) through a waitlist page. Confirm the specific product, availability and contract before assuming which party becomes the seller.


### Can an Indian SaaS Business Collect International Subscriptions with Razorpay?


Razorpay’s subscription FAQ documents card subscriptions in supported international currencies. International enablement, card support and your account configuration must be confirmed first. UPI and Emandate subscriptions are INR-only. Native billing and payment recovery do not by themselves transfer your responsibility for applicable international transaction taxes.


### Does Using a Merchant of Record Remove All Indian Compliance Work?


No. A contracted MoR can handle the transaction responsibilities it covers, but the Indian business still needs appropriate accounting and records for its own supply and receipts. Have the actual seller arrangement, invoices, payout documents and applicable export treatment reviewed. Not all MoR contracts provide identical coverage.


### Does Razorpay Provide Documents for International Receipts?


Razorpay documents downloadable FIRS records, including bank certificates and Razorpay-generated statements, plus separate bank-transfer export-document workflows. Confirm the document type and availability for the payment method you use. Keep purpose codes, buyer details and invoices aligned. A receipt document supports the audit trail; it does not alone establish export tax treatment.


### Is a Payment Gateway Always Cheaper Than a Merchant of Record?


No. Compare equivalent services and the work you retain. A gateway quote may exclude billing, tax services and operational work, while an MoR quote may bundle some of these with processing. FX, taxes on fees, refunds, dispute charges, reserves and payout terms also matter. Use actual quotes rather than headline rates.
